supports: in Curl_cookie_add the libpsl branch calls psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable(psl, domain, co->domain)
neither argument is lowercased before the call; domain is the URL host string and co->domain is the Set-Cookie domain attribute
the branch is compiled only under USE_LIBPSL
the call result is used directly as acceptable; a false result drops the cookie and a true result accepts it
the fixed branch copies both domain strings through Curl_strntolower into 256-byte buffers before the PSL check
psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable is then called with the lowercased lcase and lcookie
names longer than the local buffers skip the PSL call entirely
the comment states the PSL check requires lowercase domain name and pattern
the diff replaces the direct PSL call with lowercase copies passed to the PSL check
the commit message is "cookie: lowercase the domain names before PSL checks", Reported-by Harry Sintonen, Closes #12387
the change is confined to lib/cookie.c

field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No HTTP server, cookie jar or crafted response was executed; the finding is static. No regression test was shipped with the fix, so there was no upstream test to read either.
The PSL comparison semantics were not verified against libpsl source; the conclusion rests on the upstream advisory wording and on the fix itself lowercasing both inputs before the same call.
The flaw only exists in builds compiled with libpsl; a build without PSL drops to bad_domain() and does not take the vulnerable branch.

CWE is split: the curl advisory assigns CWE-201 (information exposure through sent data), NVD primary is NVD-CWE-noinfo, and CISA-ADP assigns CWE-178 (improper handling of case sensitivity). Both specific CWEs are recorded.
Severity agrees numerically: NVD and OSV both carry CVSS 3.1 6.5 MEDIUM, and the advisory labels it Medium. Unlike CVE-2023-38545 there is no score conflict here.

The OSV record writes the GIT range as introduced e2ae32ff and last_affected 172e54cd; those are a 7.46.0 release-notes commit and a tiny-curl patch commit after 8.4.0, not the code boundaries. The advisory GIT events and the release tags were used instead.
The 256-byte stack buffers added by the fix make names of 256 bytes or longer skip the PSL check; this is visible in the fixed source but was not analyzed as a separate weakness.

critical_operation.description: In Curl_cookie_add's USE_LIBPSL branch, the URL host `domain` and the cookie's `co->domain` attribute are passed verbatim to psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable. The PSL check requires lowercase inputs; at 8.3.0 nothing lowercases them, so `domain=co.UK` presented to a lowercase host under co.uk does not match the PSL rule and the otherwise-forbidden cookie is accepted. The 8.5.0 fix copies both strings through Curl_strntolower first.

entry_point.description: Curl_cookie_add parses a Set-Cookie header (or a cookie file line). The domain attribute is attacker-controlled by the HTTP server sending the response, and `domain` is the host curl is talking to. The PSL branch runs only when curl is built with libpsl and the cookie carries a domain attribute that is not an IP literal.

location.verification_method: Static read of lib/cookie.c at curl-8_3_0 and curl-8_5_0, the fix diff and the CURL-CVE advisory; no code executed.

trace.description: A cookie is received or loaded and Curl_cookie_add parses its domain
The mixed-case domain and cookie domain are passed to the PSL check without lower-casing
A public suffix written in mixed case is accepted, allowing a supercookie

open_questions: Whether a specific libpsl version compares locale-sensitively or by ASCII folding was not inspected in libpsl source.
No end-to-end cookie-jar experiment was run to show the supercookie being replayed to a second origin.
Whether other case-folding call sites in cookie.c have the same assumption was not audited.
